newsitem.title: THAILAND: Alphatec to issue 38.9 mln new shares.
newsitem.headline: Alphatec to issue 38.9 mln new shares.

text.p: Thai semiconductor maker, Alphatec Electronics Plc, said on Friday it planned to raise its registered capital to 803 million baht ($30.88 million) from 414 million by issuing 38.9 million new shares.
Of the new shares, 25 million shares will be offered to foreign investors through an issue of American Depository Receipts (ADRs), Alphatec said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand.
Alphatec will seek to list its planned ADRs in the New York Stock Exchange, the company said.
Other details and conditions of the ADRs would be made by the company's president, it said.
Alphatec said the proceeds from share sales to foreign investors will be used to build its new plant and repay existing convertibile debentures.
The remaining 13.9 million shares will be used to swap for the shares of NS Electronics Bangkok (1993) Co Ltd and Alphasource Manufacturing Solutions Plc.
Under the deal, one Alphatec share will be swapped for five existing shares of NS Electronics Bangkok or 6.5746 shares of Alphasource Manufacturing.
After the share swap, Alphatec will hold 99.9 percent stake in both NS Electronics and Alphasource Manufacturing, it said.
Alphatec will also spend two billion baht to buy 167 million shares of Submicron Technology Plc. After the purchase, Alphatec's holding in Submicron will rise to 46.87 percent from 2.5 percent.
The major shareholder and founder of Submicron is Charn Uswachoke, who is also the chief exective officer and major shareholder of Alphatec. ($1=26 baht)
